claim_text: A single crafted git push could achieve arbitrary server-side command execution because unsanitized push option values were inserted into internal metadata in a way that let attacker-controlled input become trusted downstream fields.
mechanism_text: User-supplied push option values entered internal metadata without sufficient sanitization. Because the metadata format used a delimiter that could also appear in user input, an attacker could inject additional fields that downstream services treated as trusted internal values. The chained injected values could then override the push-processing environment, bypass sandboxing protections, and execute arbitrary commands on the server.
bounds: This mechanism is supported by GitHub’s described root-cause and exploit chain, but the material does not independently quantify exploit reliability across products beyond the reported demonstration.

claim_text: GitHub says it reproduced the issue within 40 minutes, identified the root cause on March 4, 2026, and deployed a fix to github.com later that same day.
mechanism_text: GitHub says the remediation worked by sanitizing user-supplied push option values so they could no longer influence internal metadata fields.
bounds: This supports the response timeline and stated remediation path, but it does not by itself establish whether other adjacent metadata channels were also audited or affected.
